What’s so masterful about this organ, though,
is how carefully its designer, Nikola Bašíc, accounted
for the randomness of nature. In other organs, creating
resonant, harmonious chords requires constant control
over how forcefully air is pushed through the pipes.
But there’s no consistency to the force of waves:
some pound the shore; some just tickle it. The Sea
Organ’s design—from the pipe’s spacing to which
pitches they produce—not only accounts for that
In the wake of a passing barge, the pipes to my left
suddenly grow much more loudly, their higher pitches
nearly drowning out those on my right. Yet the overall
effect doesn’t change. The airy, round tones still twine
with the lapping of the waves. Calming my thoughts and
